answer: Network coordinate multilateration resists Sybil attacks by bounding an agent's physical location through speed-of-light packet delays. An attacker cannot anchor synthetic identities at a single hosting wharf; generating each verifiable network echo requires geographically dispersed hardware rather than replaying a cached measurement relic, imposing linear infrastructure costs. However, BGP route flapping and proxy hops inject latency jitter that can falsely penalize honest agents.
